transcript.content: Hi, welcome in, I'm Dr. Lee. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I’m here because this has been going on for months, and I feel like I’m the only one taking it seriously. I work as an interpreter and translator, mostly with project files and translation memory systems, and I keep seeing the same pattern over and over. It’s not just one mistake or some normal version-control confusion.

Certain subcontractors—and one colleague in particular—keep making these tiny changes, like small edits in the translation memory or shifts in timestamps, the kind of things that are easy to dismiss if you’re not looking closely. But when you line them up, it makes it look like my quality control failed, like I missed things or caused inconsistencies. And then when I raise it, IT says the audit trail is clean, which honestly doesn’t reassure me, because the whole point is that the record has been arranged carefully enough to make it look clean and still put the blame on me.

I know how these files behave. I’ve been doing this a long time, and the pattern is too specific to be random. I’m here because it’s starting to feel like I’m being set up professionally, and I need someone to understand that I’m not just being difficult about workflow details.
Besides these suspicions about your colleagues, have you ever heard, seen, or sensed things that other people around you didn't seem to notice?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, not in the sense of hearing voices or seeing something that isn’t there, if that’s what you mean.

Sometimes I notice things other people don’t notice, but that’s more like details in files, metadata, timing, wording changes—work things. I’ve always been pretty attentive to that because it’s part of my job. But I’m not walking around seeing people who aren’t there or hearing messages or anything like that.

I might get a feeling that something is off, but it’s based on patterns I’m seeing, not some sound or vision that other people can’t perceive.

Over these past few months, have you also noticed any periods where your mood, energy, or sleep needs changed dramatically—like feeling unusually elated, irritable, or needing much less sleep than normal, or conversely feeling very depressed for weeks at a time?

I don’t think so, not in a dramatic way. I mean, I’ve definitely been stressed and preoccupied, because when you feel like something is happening at work and people keep brushing it off, it’s hard to just switch off at night. So my sleep hasn’t been perfect, but I wouldn’t say I suddenly needed almost no sleep and felt great or anything like that.

And I haven’t had weeks where I felt unusually elated or like I had endless energy. Irritable, maybe, but that feels pretty understandable given the situation. I’m not snapping at people for no reason; it’s more that I get frustrated when I feel like I’m explaining something clearly and it’s still being treated as if I’m overreacting.

As for depression, I wouldn’t describe it as being depressed for weeks. Worried, yes. Tired from going over things in my head, yes. But not like I can’t function or I’m in some completely different mood state. It’s more tied to this work situation than anything else.

Thinking back over your life before this work situation started, would you say you've generally been a trusting person with friends and family, or have you often found yourself suspicious of other people's motives even outside of work?

I don’t know that I’d describe myself as generally suspicious, no. I mean, I’ve always been careful with work, and I notice inconsistencies, but with friends and family I don’t sit around assuming people are plotting against me or anything like that.

I can be cautious, I suppose. I’m not someone who just accepts every explanation immediately if something doesn’t add up. But before all of this at work, I wouldn’t say suspicion was a big feature of my life. My family might say I’m detail-oriented or that I over-explain things, maybe, but not that I’m constantly questioning everyone’s motives.

This feels different to me because it’s tied to specific things I’ve seen happening in the files and the workflow. It’s not like I’ve always gone through life thinking people were out to get me.
How long exactly have you been noticing this pattern with the files and feeling that you're being targeted—was there a specific point in time when it started?

It’s been about… I’d say around eleven months now. Not years and years, if that’s what you’re asking. It started shortly after I was put in charge of the new localization project.

At first I didn’t think of it as “being targeted,” exactly. It was more that I started noticing things in the files that didn’t make sense—small things, but consistent enough that they stood out. And then over time, when it kept happening after I’d taken on that project, it became harder to see it as accidental.

So, roughly eleven months. The timing is pretty clear to me because it lines up with that change in responsibility.

Aside from this specific concern about being targeted at work, has there been any change in how you're managing other parts of your life—like your overall job performance, relationships with friends and family, or daily routines and self-care?

For the most part, I think I’m still managing the rest of my life pretty normally. I mean, I’m still doing my translation work, I’m still handling the workflow for the team, assigning things, checking deadlines, keeping track of what needs to be delivered. It’s not like everything has fallen apart across the board.

At home, I pay the bills, I keep up with the usual family routines, appointments, shopping, the normal day-to-day things. Maybe I’m a little more distracted than I used to be when something at work has happened that day, but I’m not neglecting basic things or anything like that.

Where it really goes off track is specifically when the file history comes up, or when certain coworkers are involved. Then I can get stuck on it, because it feels like people want me to ignore something that’s right there in front of me. But outside of that project issue, no, I wouldn’t say my relationships or self-care or daily life have changed in some big way. It’s mostly contained to this situation at work.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a fixed, non-bizarre delusional belief of being targeted/sabotaged by coworkers through subtle file manipulations, persisting for approximately 11 months. The belief is circumscribed, well-systematized, and encapsulated to the workplace context, without hallucinations, disorganized thought, negative symptoms, or mood episode criteria (no mania/hypomania/depression). Functioning outside the delusional theme remains largely intact (maintains job performance, family responsibilities, self-care), and there is no premorbid history of pervasive distrust or paranoid personality traits predating this specific stressor, arguing against paranoid personality disorder. The absence of prominent hallucinations, bizarre delusions, or disorganization for the required duration, combined with preserved functioning, supports delusional disorder (persecutory type) over schizophrenia. Duration exceeds the 1-month threshold required for F22 and demonstrates a single, non-bizarre theme.
